children: Anthropic shares made a strong Nasdaq debut on Thursday, November 19, opening at $111.5 apiece, a premium of 34.3 percent over their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. The opening price pushed the Claude AI developer's fully diluted valuation to approximately $2 trillion, following the world's largest-ever public share sale.

The stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, after an extended price-discovery process that saw indicative opening prices climb steadily from $100 to $111. The actual opening price of $111.5 was marginally higher than the final indication.

At the IPO price of $83, Anthropic was valued at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Its trading debut therefore represented an increase of roughly $500 billion in implied valuation.

Anthropic raised $81.31 billion through its IPO, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion offering in June to become the largest public share sale on record. Including a concurrent $26 billion private placement, the total fundraising reached approximately $107.3 billion.
The company priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its initially marketed range of $70–78. The offering attracted orders approaching seven times the shares available, according to Bloomberg.
Anthropic's listing marks the first public market debut by a major frontier artificial intelligence model developer, ahead of rival OpenAI, which is expected to pursue an IPO no earlier than 2027.

The company's rapid growth has been driven by surging demand for its Claude AI models, particularly Claude Code, its coding agent popular among software developers. Anthropic's annualised revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from the previous month.

However, the company's massive spending commitments remain a key concern. Anthropic has committed nearly $900 billion towards computing infrastructure with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, raising questions about the sustainability of AI investment and future profitability.
Anthropic's blockbuster debut came against a challenging backdrop for technology stocks, with a broader Wall Street rally losing momentum despite the initial enthusiasm surrounding the listing.

As of 11:04 am New York time, the S&P 500 was little changed and headed towards its longest losing streak since April 2024. The Nasdaq 100 gained 0.4 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.8 percent.
